title: FFIEC publishes formal booklet addendum on agentic-AI developer-tool exposure by mid-July 2026
body: By mid-July 2026 the FFIEC interagency cohort (OCC, Federal Reserve Board, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB) publishes a formal addendum to its Outsourced Technology Services examination booklet establishing supervisory expectations for federally-regulated financial institutions' use of agentic-AI developer tooling, accelerated from the prior Q3 2026 expected guidance timeline that was signalled in the FFIEC's Tuesday outsourced-technology examination note. The trigger is the Thursday joint statement issued by the same FFIEC cohort flagging that the second-consecutive-trading-week confirmed-exploitation pattern across three orchestrator vendors (OpenAI Codex CLI CVE-2026-46127 Tuesday, Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 CVE-2026-46198 Wednesday, Mistral Workflows CVE-2026-46341 Thursday) meets the booklet-addendum threshold the Tuesday note had pre-identified, with CISA placing CVE-2026-46341 on the KEV catalog Thursday afternoon after Mandiant confirmed a third Fortune 500 incident-response engagement at an industrial-manufacturing customer — taking the cohort vertical-count to three (financial services, healthcare, industrial manufacturing) and the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy to fourteen catalogued instances. The most likely landing is an early-July formal addendum draft circulated to the cohort regulators ahead of a mid-July joint publication, naming three supervisory expectations: documented enforcement of vendor force-roll patch windows under a 48-hour SLA across agentic-orchestrator tenancies; board-level attestation that the institution's agentic-AI tool inventory has been mapped against the Trail of Bits taxonomy with mitigation status tracked per CVE; and a third-party-risk-management workstream covering the cross-orchestrator interop matrix (Mistral Workflows plus OpenAI Codex CLI plus Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 plus Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog plus Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center) that Mistral's Thursday GA cut crystallised as the canonical cross-vendor baseline. Bear case is one of the five FFIEC member agencies dissents on scope (most likely the CFPB on the agentic-AI consumer-finance carve-out) and the joint publication slips into the August examiner-cycle window; absent that dissent, mid-July 2026 lands the first US federal banking-supervision rulebook entry explicitly naming agentic-AI developer tooling as an outsourced-technology examination focus area.

reasoning.because: FFIEC Thursday joint statement explicitly named booklet-addendum threshold as crossed
reasoning.given: Three orchestrator CVEs across three verticals in two trading weeks plus Mandiant Fortune 500 IR
reasoning.so_that: Federal banking supervision gets first rulebook entry naming agentic-AI dev tooling as exam focus
reasoning.landing: Formal addendum draft early-July, joint publication by 2026-07-17
reasoning.plain_language: US bank regulators will rush new AI-tool exam rules out by mid-July after this week's hacks.

summary: Three AI coding tools got hacked this week across three industries, so US banking regulators will rush out new examination rules for banks using AI dev tools by mid-July.
